csv_scope_of_work: Estero River Park is an initiative aimed at preserving natural landscapes while enhancing recreational and commercial opportunities. The long-range vision for the Eco-Historical Hub is to provide a variety of unique, high-quality recreational, educational, cultural, residential and commercial experiences for Estero residents and visitors while preserving, protecting, and enhancing the hub s unique environmental and cultural resources. Activities may include: Concerts and Performances Casual Waterfront Dining Canoeing/Kayaking Environmentally sensitive residential, commercial, and/or institutional development Others The Village is advancing the strategic redevelopment of the 32-acre publicly owned site within the Eco-Historical Hub located north of the river. This initiative envisions the creation of a vertically integrated mixed-use development anchored by multifamily residential and activated by complementary ground-floor retail and neighborhoodserving commercial space. The proposed Bonita Estero Rail Trail (BERT) will run from Wiggins Pass Road in Collier County border along the 11.4 miles unused rail corridor through downtown Bonita Springs and Estero ending at Estero Parkway. The Village-owned 32-acre tract north of the river presents an opportunity for the potential development of a gated residential neighborhood within the hub that will be centered around single-family homes. The mixed-use portion of the proposed development will create an activated, river-oriented area where residents live above restaurants, caf s, and retail spaces in a cohesive pedestrian-friendly environment. The design emphasizes connectivity, outdoor gathering areas, and a continuous level of activity throughout the day and evening. The Village of Estero is seeking qualified development partners to collaborate on the master planning, development, financing, and long-term operation of a 32-acre Village-owned site located north of the Estero River

project_scope: Public-private partnership for strategic redevelopment of a 32-acre Village-owned site north of the Estero River within the Eco-Historical Hub. The vision includes a vertically integrated mixed-use development with multifamily residential above ground-floor retail and neighborhood-serving commercial uses, plus a potential gated residential neighborhood centered on single-family homes. The broader hub vision mentions recreational, educational, cultural, residential, and commercial uses and connectivity to the proposed 11.4-mile Bonita Estero Rail Trail corridor.
services: Development partner services for master planning, development, financing, and long-term operation; design-build/developer services; construction/project management; housing and urban development; redevelopment planning.
relevance_explanation:
- Primarily a developer/master planning P3 opportunity, not a structural engineering or bridge design tender.
- Focus is mixed-use urban redevelopment, housing, retail, financing, and operations.
- No defined building, bridge, roof, or special structural scope with technical parameters.
- Includes project management and redevelopment planning components, which are generally low relevance for sbp.
- Possible future buildings could emerge, but current procurement stage is too broad and non-technical.

Available scope information: 32-acre redevelopment site north of the Estero River; mixed-use development with multifamily residential, ground-floor retail/commercial, and potential single-family gated neighborhood; long-term operation under a P3 model. This is insufficient for a realistic construction cost estimate.
fee_explanation: No fee information is provided. Because the procurement is for a development partner covering master planning, development, financing, and operation rather than a defined structural engineering scope, no realistic sbp fee estimate can be derived.
